The record:
Write the postmortem for the incident below.

Alert: HighErrorRate on io-shop
What the alert said [AL1]: Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}
Alert raised: 2026-11-11T04:35:34Z {alert_raised}
Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one. An alert rule fires; a person is paged. Argus first posted about the incident in Slack at 2026-11-11T04:35:57Z {first_told}, and the document says so already: leave that post out, and do not say that no person was told. That nobody was paged is a finding of its own.
The alert rule waits 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding before it fires. The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds {accounted_for} accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute {rule_evaluated_every}, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds {scraping_allowance} for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
Broken from 2026-11-11T04:29:00Z {began} (the onset, dated to its minute: a change came during that minute) to 2026-11-11T04:41:00Z {back_to_normal}, when the metrics show it back to normal.
That is 12 minutes {duration}, and every impact figure below is measured over that stretch.
Argus held the incident for 6 minutes 19 seconds {held}, until 2026-11-11T04:42:14Z {argus_stopped}. That is not how long the fault lasted, nor how long Argus went on working - leave it out of your answer.
The service's error rate over all its requests, before it began: 1.0% {errors_before}.
The same rate while it was broken: 29.3% {errors_while_broken}, peaking at 35.5% {errors_at_worst}.
Rise above baseline: 28.3% {errors_rise} of traffic failed that otherwise would not have.
The series behind the alert, `sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[1m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[1m]))` - its alert said "Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}" - which its alert rule evaluates and calls worse rising: 1.0416666666666666% {series_before} before it began, 29.333333333333333% {series_while_broken} on average while it was broken, and 35.5% {series_at_worst} at its worst. Say what it measures in words, not by its query.
Customer loss: 7,533.46 USD {customer_loss} - how far the shop's takings over the incident fell short of the same hours whole weeks earlier, beyond how much those hours vary on their own.

I ranked legacy-checkout-fallback second.
  - [T16] 2026-11-11T04:37:21Z {T16.1} Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 2 {T16.2} flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 {T16.3} hour before 04:37:21 {T16.4}

  - [T26] 2026-11-11T04:40:39Z {T26.1} Mitigation Agent: Waiting to see whether the service is still at the incident's level, from 04:41 {T26.2} - up to 149s {T26.3}
  - [T27] 2026-11-11T04:42:14Z {T27.1} Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - no longer at the incident's level since 04:41 {T27.2}
  - [T28] 2026-11-11T04:42:14Z {T28.1} Mitigation Agent: Judged the action CONFIRMED
  - [T29] 2026-11-11T04:42:14Z {T29.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATED - set flag [legacy-checkout-fallback] ON and the rule that fired stopped firing
  - [T30] 2026-11-11T04:43:55Z {T30.1} Code-Fix Agent: Proposed a fix as a draft pull request - https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/560
A person's message never stops a step already running: between steps, Argus starts no new one while a message waits to be answered.

Changes to production it read:
  - [P1] 2026-11-11T04:29:13Z {P1.1} flag-toggle legacy-checkout-fallback by admin: feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback was switched off
  - [P2] 2026-11-11T04:29:13Z {P2.1} flag-toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
  - Deploys read, none came back.

Log lines it read, one per message:
  - [G153f] INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=on - 200 {G153f.1} evaluations - 3 {G153f.2} occurrences in 3 {G153f.3} minutes, 04:26–04:28 {G153f.4}
  - [G7e5d] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 {G7e5d.1} evaluations - 3 {G7e5d.2} occurrences in 3 {G7e5d.3} minutes, 04:26–04:28 {G7e5d.4}
  - [Gc27d] INFO io-shop: account pages served - # by the legacy renderer, # by the new renderer - 10 {Gc27d.1} occurrences in 10 {Gc27d.2} minutes, 04:26–04:35 {Gc27d.3}; # was 0 {Gc27d.4} to 200 {Gc27d.5}, typically 0 {Gc27d.6}, highest at 04:26 {Gc27d.7}; # was 0 {Gc27d.8} to 200 {Gc27d.9}, typically 200 {Gc27d.10}, highest at 04:30 {Gc27d.11}
  - [G46bc] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 6 {G46bc.1} occurrences in 3 {G46bc.2} minutes, 04:26–04:28 {G46bc.3}
  - [Gbac1] WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 10 {Gbac1.1} occurrences in 10 {Gbac1.2} minutes, 04:26–04:35 {Gbac1.3}; # was 1.00% {Gbac1.4} to 33.00% {Gbac1.5}, typically 26.50% {Gbac1.6}, highest at 04:35 {Gbac1.7}
  - [G7ad6] INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=off 152 {G7ad6.1} / on 48 {G7ad6.2} - 200 {G7ad6.3} evaluations - 1 {G7ad6.4} occurrence in 1 {G7ad6.5} minute, 04:29 {G7ad6.6}
  - [G971b] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 47 {G971b.1} / on 153 {G971b.2} - 200 {G971b.3} evaluations - 1 {G971b.4} occurrence in 1 {G971b.5} minute, 04:29 {G971b.6}
  - [G5309] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 {G5309.1} occurrences in 7 {G5309.2} minutes, 04:29–04:35 {G5309.3}
  - [G7037] INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=off - 200 {G7037.1} evaluations - 6 {G7037.2} occurrences in 6 {G7037.3} minutes, 04:30–04:35 {G7037.4}
  - [Gce95] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 {Gce95.1} evaluations - 6 {Gce95.2} occurrences in 6 {Gce95.3} minutes, 04:30–04:35 {Gce95.4}

Candidates it considered, in the Investigator's words - name them by their labels, but cite none; what they claim is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [C1] At 2026-11-11T04:29:13Z {C1.1} the monthly-spend-feature flag was switched on, enabling the spend summary path. It raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 and fails about 30% {C1.2} of account page requests. No deployment or code change was involved. [feature-flag-toggle, confidence 0.55 {C1.3}, refuted]
  - [C2] At 2026-11-11T04:29:13Z {C2.1} the legacy-checkout-fallback flag was switched off. Account pages moved from the legacy renderer to the new renderer, and the new renderer's spend summary raises ZeroDivisionError. [feature-flag-toggle, confidence 0.4 {C2.2}, confirmed]

Actions it took:
  - [M1] Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for [C1] (can be put back) - refuted, put back when it did not help
  - [M2] Reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback for [C2] (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix, and what it claims is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [F1] The fault is in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, in `average_spend_per_item_this_month`: `account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month)` (line 47 {F1.1}, the line the investigation's errors point to). The divisor is the number of purchases this account made in the current month. A shopper who has bought before but not this month makes that zero, and that is an ordinary shopper: the test file's own fixture calls this "the ordinary case". Each request that `render_spend_summary` sends down the monthly path (`use_monthly_summary=True`) for such a shopper raises ZeroDivisionError. `serve_account_page` in src/io_shop/account_page.py catches it and returns a failed page. Turning the legacy-checkout-fallback flag off sent more account pages down this new path. That exposed the fault; the flag did not cause it. With the code as it stands, the flag cannot safely be turned off again.
      
      The fix: when there are no purchases this month, the function returns 0 {F1.2}, meaning no spend this month, and does not divide. Shoppers who did buy this month take the same path as before. The lifetime average and its deliberate ZeroDivisionError for an account with no history at all are unchanged, so the existing boundary tests that rely on that error still hold. The line-number test also still holds, because it goes through the lifetime function, whose lines this change does not move. No error is swallowed: the guard checks the one known empty case and returns a defined figure for it.
      
      The new tests in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py cover a shopper with past purchases and none this month. They call the function directly and also through `render_spend_summary` with `use_monthly_summary=True`, and assert 0 {F1.3}. Against the current code both would raise ZeroDivisionError.
  - Say what the files Code-Fix read do, with the conditions it gives - a default as a default, never as all it does - and no wider: 'nothing in the files it read', never 'nothing in the code'.

Action items the record already holds:
  - AI-1 (mitigate, done): Reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback
  - AI-2 (prevent, open): Review and merge the proposed fix
PR #560 is a draft Argus opened for a person to review and merge. The record holds nothing about it after that: do not say it was reviewed, approved or merged, or that it was not - nor that the record holds nothing, which the document says itself. Nothing ran its test or its fix: say what it proposes, not that it corrects anything.
The document already states what set it off, in a section of its own: the change [P1].

Cite evidence in causal_chain by its label. In a contributing factor's addressed_by, name the record's own action items that answer it, by their number; an item you propose names the factors it answers in its answers, by their labels.

What people working the incident wrote in its thread:
  - L1 (Some Person, 2026-11-11T04:36:21Z): "it's legacy-checkout-fallback - someone switched it off right before this started" - the investigation found it unverified: The flag was switched off at 2026-11-11T04:29:13Z, but monthly-spend-feature was switched on at the same moment and the errors are ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py:47, so which flag caused it is not settled. I ranked legacy-checkout-fallback second.
Each was weighed on what the investigation had read, before anything was tried. Where the actions above say otherwise, the actions are the later word.
For each, say in lead_effects whether it changed what was done.

Call submit_postmortem with your answer.

The document, by field:
root_cause: In the files Code-Fix read, the new renderer's monthly spend summary (`average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, line {F1.1}) divides the account's spend this month by the number of purchases it made this month, and nothing guards against that count being zero. So for any shopper who has bought before but not this month it raises ZeroDivisionError, and `serve_account_page` catches the error and returns a failed page. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
cause_in_plain_words: Switching off a setting moved the shop's account pages onto newer code that likely breaks for any shopper who has bought before but not this month, because it tries to work out an average over zero purchases.
still_at_risk: If legacy-checkout-fallback is turned off again, account pages could go back onto the new renderer and fail again for shoppers with no purchases this month.
symptom: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
lead_effects L1: It did not change what was done: the investigation weighed it as unverified and ranked legacy-checkout-fallback second, so that flag was reverted only after the revert of monthly-spend-feature was refuted.
causal_chain 1: Shoppers' account page requests failed: the service's own account-page error-rate warning rose from its usual level, and the error-rate alert fired. (cites Gbac1, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; AL1)
causal_chain 2: Account page requests were raising ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py from the onset minute ({G5309.3}), and the account page handler turned each one into a failed page. (cites G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; F1, under "What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix")
causal_chain 3: Account pages had moved from the legacy renderer to the new renderer, whose spend summary runs the line that raised. The legacy renderer's count was highest at {Gc27d.7} and the new renderer's at {Gc27d.11}. (cites Gc27d, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; F1, under "What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix")
causal_chain 4: The legacy-checkout-fallback flag was switched off at {P1.1}. Flag evaluations went from all on before the onset to mostly off in the onset minute, and then to all off. (cites P1, under "Changes to production it read"; G153f, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G7ad6, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G7037, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 4 ruled_out 1: The monthly-spend-feature flag, switched on at the same instant ({P2.1}): turning it off left the service at the incident's level, and the service came back with it still on once legacy-checkout-fallback was turned back on. (cites T19, under "What Argus did, in order"; T21, under "What Argus did, in order"; T22, under "What Argus did, in order"; T25, under "What Argus did, in order"; T27, under "What Argus did, in order"; T28, under "What Argus did, in order")
causal_chain 5: The new renderer's spend summary divides by the number of purchases the shopper made this month, and Code-Fix's reading of the source says that number is zero for an ordinary shopper who has not bought this month. (cites F1, under "What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix"; G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
contributing_factors 1: No check was seen that tested the new renderer's spend summary with an account that has past purchases but none this month before a flag could send production account pages to it. Code-Fix's reading says the test file's own fixture calls such a shopper the ordinary case.
contributing_factors 1 had_it_been_otherwise: The divide-by-zero would have been found before the flag was switched off, and account pages would not have been sent to a path that fails for ordinary shoppers.
contributing_factors 2: Switching off legacy-checkout-fallback moved all account page traffic to the new renderer within the onset minute. No staged rollout of the flag change to a small share of traffic was seen.
contributing_factors 2 had_it_been_otherwise: Only a small share of account pages would have failed while the change was judged, and the rollout could have been stopped before it reached everyone.
contributing_factors 3: Two flags on the same service were changed by the same actor at the same instant, so the investigation could not tell from the record which one caused the errors.
contributing_factors 3 had_it_been_otherwise: The flag that set it off would have been the only change in the window, so the first revert would have targeted it and the incident would have ended sooner.
action_items 1: Before a feature flag on io-shop can send production traffic onto a new code path, require that path's tests to pass against ordinary account data, including an account with past purchases but none this month.
action_items 2: Roll out io-shop feature flag changes to a small share of traffic first, and widen them only after the error rate holds.
action_items 3: Stop a staged flag rollout on io-shop automatically and revert it when the service's error rate rises during the rollout.
action_items 4: Change feature flags on io-shop one at a time, with an observation window between changes.
action_items 5: Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop so that it pages the on-call engineer.
action_items 6: Keep legacy-checkout-fallback on until the fix under review in AI-2 is merged and deployed, and record that hold where flag owners will see it.
went_wrong 1: The person's lead in the thread named the right flag before the investigation began, but the investigation ranked that flag second. The first revert went to the wrong flag, and the right one waited until that revert was judged.
went_wrong 2: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to the alert.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {T5.1} or {duration}, are figures code writes in from the row they name. They are not judged.
  - Action items propose what to do; they make no claim about the record.
  - Whether something went well, went wrong or was lucky is a judgement. Only a fact it states is judged.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.

tools.name: judge_claims
